articles.title: 1. Definitions

paragraphs: CommonLink is a donation platform enabling associations, foundations, endowment funds, NGOs and corporate donors to collect, track and document the use of collected funds, with transparency and proof-of-use mechanisms.
The Platform enables in particular:
articles.title: 2. Service description

CommonLink is not a payment institution. Payment services are provided by authorised providers.
Donations are made directly for the benefit of beneficiary organisations. CommonLink does not legally collect the funds for its own account.

complaints.intro: You are not satisfied with a service provided by CommonLink, with information you received, or with how your request was handled. This page explains how to let us know and what happens next.

paragraphs: A complaint is the expression of dissatisfaction with us. You don’t need to use the word "complaint," or to ask for anything in particular.
You also don't need to have made a donation, or to have an account. Anyone can send us a complaint.
On the other hand, a request for information, an explanation, or assistance is not a complaint. For these requests, simply write to us at contact@common-link.org
sections.title: What is a complaint

items: By mail, to CommonLink, Complaints Department, 1047 Chemin des Impiniers, 06220 Vallauris, France

By phone, at +33 4 23 40 02 06, standard rate from a landline. If we cannot respond to your request immediately, we will ask you to confirm it in writing. The timeframes below then run from your written confirmation.
paragraphs: If you send your complaint to another one of our contacts, it will be forwarded to our complaints service. You will not need to repeat your request.
sections.title: How to reach us

paragraphs: Provide your name, a way to reach you, and describe what dissatisfied you. If your complaint concerns a specific donation or campaign, please specify it — that will save us both time.
sections.title: To help us handle your request

sections.callout: These two timeframes run from when you send your complaint, not from the date we become aware of it. For mail, the postmark serves as proof.
paragraphs: We acknowledge receipt of your written complaint within a maximum of ten business days. If we are able to provide you with a final response directly within this period, we do not send a separate acknowledgment of receipt.
We respond to you in writing, with reasons, within a maximum of two months.
paragraphsAfter: When your complaint concerns an urgent situation, we adapt this timeframe to the nature of your request.
sections.title: Our timeframes

paragraphs: You retain the right to bring the matter before the competent courts.
sections.title: If our response does not satisfy you

paragraphs: Every complaint is logged and tracked through to its closure.

We review them regularly to identify what needs to be corrected in our services. When a complaint reveals an error that may have affected people other than you, we extend the correction to everyone concerned.
sections.title: What we do with your complaint

paragraphs: The information you provide us as part of a complaint is used to process it and kept for five years from the closing of the case. Details are set out in our privacy policy.
sections.title: Your data

faq.intro: Find below answers to the most frequently asked questions about CommonLink.

q0.a: CommonLink is a donation platform enabling associations, foundations, endowment funds, NGOs and corporate donors to collect, track and document the use of collected funds, with transparency and proof-of-use mechanisms.

q1.a: CommonLink is aimed at associations, foundations, endowment funds, NGOs, corporate donors, and donors wishing to track how their funds are used. The service targets the French market at launch.

q10.a: In principle, a donation is final and non-refundable. A refund may however be considered in cases of double payment, manifest error, fraud, unauthorised payment, cancelled campaign or beneficiary organisation removed from the Platform. Requests should be sent to contact@common-link.org.

q11.a: Unless stated otherwise, the donation is legally vested in the beneficiary organisation upon receipt, regardless of whether the displayed goal is reached.
q11.q: What happens if a campaign does not reach its goal?

q12.a: The donation is made directly for the benefit of the beneficiary organisation. CommonLink does not legally collect the funds for its own account.

q13.a: CommonLink charges beneficiary organisations 8% excl. VAT in service fees and 2% in payment and technical processing fees, invoiced monthly. The donor may also leave an optional voluntary contribution. See the Pricing page for details.
q13.q: Does CommonLink take a commission on donations?

q14.a: When the beneficiary organisation is eligible, tax receipts are generated by CommonLink on behalf of the beneficiary organisation. They may be sent by email and/or made available in the donor's account.

q15.a: No. A digital certificate, NFT or complementary proof element does not constitute a tax receipt. A tax receipt is a separate document, generated on behalf of the beneficiary organisation when applicable conditions are met.
q15.q: Is the digital certificate or NFT a tax receipt?

q16.a: No. CommonLink does not guarantee the final use of funds by the beneficiary organisation. CommonLink provides transparency tools to track certain financial flows and present proof of use.
q16.q: Does CommonLink guarantee how funds are used?

q17.a: Proof of use refers to elements that document how funds were used: recorded transactions, submitted supporting documents, technical or blockchain data when these features are activated. These elements do not constitute exhaustive accounting or legal certification.

q18.a: Certain CommonLink features may use blockchain technologies, including Polygon, to contribute to the transparency and documentation of flows.

q19.a: Yes. CommonLink may use Monerium's services for certain features related to electronic money, EURe and flow transparency. Monerium is an authorised electronic money institution.

q2.a: Yes. CommonLink is a social and solidarity economy company. An ESUS accreditation application has been submitted.
q2.q: Is CommonLink a social and solidarity economy company?

q20.a: Yes. CommonLink may refuse, suspend or remove a beneficiary organisation or campaign in particular in cases of inaccurate information, KYC/KYB refusal, suspicion of fraud, serious dispute or legal risk.
q20.q: Can CommonLink refuse or suspend an organisation?

q21.a: At launch, CommonLink uses only cookies strictly necessary for the Site to function. Analytics, marketing or advertising cookies are not active at launch. See the Cookie Policy.

q22.a: Email: contact@common-link.org — Phone: +33 4 23 40 02 06. CommonLink aims to respond within 48 business hours.

q23.a: To exercise your rights regarding your personal data, write to legal@common-link.org. CommonLink aims to respond within 7 business days.
q23.q: How do I exercise my GDPR rights?

q3.a: CommonLink is registered with ORIAS under number 26010395 as an intermediary in participatory financing.

q4.a: No. CommonLink is not a payment institution. Payment services are provided by authorised providers.

q5.a: The donor creates an account, selects a campaign, makes a donation, receives a payment confirmation and can track their donation from their account. When applicable conditions are met, a tax receipt is generated by CommonLink on behalf of the beneficiary organisation.

q6.a: No. Creating an account is required to make a donation via CommonLink.
q6.q: Can I donate without creating an account?

q7.a: No. The donor chooses a campaign but does not choose a detailed individual allocation of funds. The allocation is global to the selected campaign.
q7.q: Can I choose exactly how my donation is used?

q8.a: Donations are one-off at launch. Recurring donation features may be offered later.

q9.a: At launch, CommonLink plans to accept bank cards and SEPA direct debit. Other payment methods may be added later.

paragraphs: The donor pays a sum of money to the beneficiary organisation, without consideration and with donative intent, to support the campaign they have chosen.
articles.title: 1. Purpose of the donation

paragraphs: The donation is a voluntary and irrevocable act. It vests in the beneficiary organisation upon receipt and is not refundable.
articles.title: 2. Final nature of the donation

paragraphs: The donor acquires no rights over the funded project. They cannot demand its completion, claim a share of its results, request the return of their donation, or obtain any form of consideration.
articles.title: 3. No rights over the project

paragraphs: The beneficiary organisation undertakes to account for the use of collected funds, by making the payments funded by the campaign from the platform and by publishing a report at its closing.
This undertaking is an information obligation. It constitutes neither a guarantee that the project will be completed nor an obligation of result.
articles.title: 4. The organisation's duty to account

paragraphs: The beneficiary organisation issues the tax receipt. It is solely responsible for its eligibility for the patronage tax regime and for the accuracy of the document.

CommonLink provides it with an issuing tool and forwards the receipt to the donor on its behalf. It does not verify the organisation’s eligibility and guarantees neither the validity of the receipt nor the granting of a tax reduction.
articles.title: 5. Tax receipt

paragraphs: Amounts paid by the donor are collected into an account opened in the beneficiary organisation's name, then transferred to its bank account. They never pass through CommonLink.
articles.title: 6. The funds

paragraphs: The beneficiary organisation is aware of the donor's identity, in particular to issue their tax receipt. It may make no other use of it than those related to this obligation and to its relationship with its donors.
The donor may choose not to appear publicly on the campaign page.
articles.title: 7. The donor's data

paragraphs: A complaint about the service provided by CommonLink is addressed to its complaints service, whose contact details appear at the top of this document.
A complaint about the use of funds or about the project itself is a matter for the beneficiary organisation.

asso.billedText: Based on donations collected during the month. Paid by bank transfer, no later than the end of the following month.
asso.flowNote: The commission is never deducted from donations. It is billed separately, at month end.
asso.soloText: You can stop using CommonLink at any time, and you only pay for the months you actually raised funds.
asso.subNote: The payment provider’s fees are included in the commission and are never re-billed.

donor.badge: CommonLink never holds funds and never deducts anything from donations.
donor.label: For donors
donor.text1: One hundred percent of your donation goes to the association. Your receipt covers the full amount.
donor.text2: CommonLink is paid by the association, at 10% ex-VAT of what it raises. Never by you.
donor.title: You pay no fees at all

hero.bigLine1: of the amount of donations raised
hero.bigLine2: billed at month end, never deducted from donations
hero.label: Pricing
hero.subtitle: No subscription, no setup fee, no per-transaction fee. You only pay in months when you actually raise funds.
hero.title: One single commission.

items: A project with an unlawful purpose.
A dissolved structure, or one whose assets are subject to a freezing order.

Funding a political party, a candidate, or an electoral campaign. The law reserves this type of funding for a specific channel, with a financial agent and receipts issued under the supervision of the national campaign accounts commission, which we do not handle. On the other hand, an association advocating for a cause — including seeking to change a law or public policy — is fully welcome.
cards.title: The law forbids it

items: A collection for the benefit of an identified individual or family. A tax receipt requires that the donation serve a general interest, not an individual situation. That's what distinguishes a donation from a whip-round.
A collection that promises the donor something in exchange for their donation — an item, a place, a service. On CommonLink, a donation entitles you to nothing other than the tax receipt.
cards.title: It would jeopardize the donor's tax receipt

items: Funding the practice of a religion, for example maintaining a place of worship or paying a minister of religion. The social, educational, or cultural activities of a religious association remain eligible.
Funding an identified individual's legal costs.
A collection that in reality funds a commercial activity.
cards.title: We chose not to accept it

exclus.label: Exclusions
exclus.title: What we don't fund
exclus.withdrawText1: A published campaign can be withdrawn if it falls under an excluded case.
exclus.withdrawText2: From your account, on a campaign page, you can flag what seems problematic to you and explain it freely. The report goes directly to our compliance team.
exclus.withdrawText3: We review it against the excluded cases described above. The association is informed of the decision, may present its observations, and may contest it. Every withdrawal is logged with its reason and date.
exclus.withdrawText4: If you don't have an account, write to us at contact@common-link.org

fonds.callout: A campaign's goal is not a threshold to cross. An association that has raised €8,000 out of a €10,000 goal has those €8,000 and can use them as soon as they are transferred. A donation belongs to it as soon as it is received.
fonds.capText1: The goal is also a cap. A campaign does not raise more than the need it announced.
fonds.capText2: Once the cap is reached, the campaign no longer accepts donations. A donation that would exceed this cap is not collected: you are informed before any payment, and we suggest another project from the same association or a comparable one.
fonds.closeText1: The association publishes a closing report accounting for the use of funds.
fonds.closeText2: If part of the funds was not spent, for example because the project cost less than expected, those funds remain the association's, and it states in its report what it does with them. They are not returned to donors: a donation is final as soon as it is received.
fonds.label: Fund circulation
fonds.spendText1: A campaign’s expenses are charged against donations received in the order they arrived, oldest first.
fonds.spendText2: An association can only commit, from CommonLink, the amounts actually available for the campaign in question.
fonds.spendTitle: How expenses are attributed to a campaign
fonds.text1: Donations are collected into an account opened in the association's name, then transferred to its bank account. No payout is conditional on reaching the fundraising goal.
fonds.text2: The payout schedule depends on the payment method chosen by the donor. The association can see, at any time from its dashboard, the amounts pending and the amounts available.
fonds.title: How funds reach the association

hero.label: Transparency
hero.text: We ask associations for no supporting documents and verify no invoices. What we publish are the payments they make from the platform, with their recipient and amount.
hero.title: Who can raise funds,

qui.acceptText1: CommonLink does not judge the merit of a project and ranks no cause above another. Our role is to verify that a campaign is presented completely, and that it does not fall under an excluded case.
qui.acceptText2: A campaign cannot be published without the following five elements, and this check is automatic.
qui.checkCallout: You enter your project’s projected budget directly in the campaign form. No document is required: no balance sheet, no income statement, no invoice, no expense receipt, no activity report.
qui.checkText: Before any fundraising, we verify the existence and identity of your structure against public registers. To do so, we collect your name, registered office address, legal form, national association register number or SIREN number, the identity of your legal representative, and your bank details.
qui.checkTitle: What we check and what we ask of you
criteriaItems: The projected budget for the use of funds
qui.generalInterest: A project must address a need of general interest, whether it benefits individuals, legal entities, animals, or the environment.
qui.intro: CommonLink is open to declared associations holding a registration number in the national register of associations, and to endowment funds, established in France.
qui.label: Eligibility
noItems: Structures dissolved or in the process of being dissolved
